title: Nuevo Laredo Leads All of Mexico in Customs Traffic — 526,871 Movements in October Alone

content:
Nuevo Laredo is now the busiest customs port in all of Mexico. The city's customs office recorded 526,871 customs movements in October 2026 — 26.5 percent of the entire country's total — putting it in first place nationally, according to data from Mexico's National Customs Agency (ANAM).

Nuevo Laredo also led the country in customs declarations, known as pedimentos, with 211,173 documents filed in October — 22 percent of all pedimentos registered in Mexico during the same period, according to El Congresista, citing Hoy Tamaulipas.

Elsewhere in Tamaulipas, the Reynosa customs office ranked fourth in the country in operations, with 103,097 movements, while Altamira and Matamoros ranked eighth and ninth in revenue collection.

Tamaulipas Secretary of Economy Anabell Flores Garza said the numbers show the strength of the state's commercial activity and the logistics infrastructure at its border crossings and ports. "The state's geographic location and its connectivity with the United States are key elements to attract international trade companies," she said, according to the report.

The state government is pushing the creation of industrial parks in Nuevo Laredo, Reynosa and Altamira to strengthen investment opportunities, improve supply chains and generate jobs, according to the report. Tamaulipas currently has five border customs offices and two seaport customs offices, along with highway corridors that move goods across the region.

Compared with previous years, the growth in Nuevo Laredo's customs operations is a positive indicator for Tamaulipas' economy and its integration into international trade, according to the report.

Sources: El Congresista, Nov. 23, 2026, with information from Hoy Tamaulipas; data from Mexico's National Customs Agency (ANAM).
